title: When the Letters Burns
premise: Eleven years ago, Wendell Oyelaran left his hometown the night before a festival, abandoning his first love, Imani, and a letter he never mailed. When a demolition notice forces him back and the letter surfaces—burned at one corner but legible—he must confront the lie he told himself: that he left to protect her, when really he left because belonging terrified him more than losing her. As he rebuilds her failing bakery beside his own café, the two become rivals, then reluctant partners, then something neither can contain. At the festival's closing night, Wendell publicly reads the scorched letter, forgives the man in the mirror, and chooses to stay—winning the bakery, the town, and Imani, not by fixing the past but by finally inhabiting the present.
about_author: R. M. Marchetti is the pen name of a former line cook turned novelist who writes love stories set in kitchens, where tenderness is measured in small, repeatable acts. They live near the coast with a sourdough starter older than most of their friendships.

chapters.title: Three Missed Payments
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. A final notice arrives at his struggling café on the same morning a demolition letter from his hometown does. He trains his hands through muscle memory, refusing to feel. Emotional beat: dread disguised as routine; the reader sees a man who has organized his whole life around not wanting things.

chapters.title: The Return Ticket
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. He goes home to sign papers, telling himself it's a forty-eight-hour errand. The town remembers him too warmly, too specifically. He glimpses Imani's bakery—flour-dusted, thriving, hers. Emotional beat: the vertigo of being known; every friendly face is a mirror he didn't ask for.

chapters.title: What the Fire Kept
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Clearing his mother's attic, he finds the letter he wrote Imani eleven years ago, corner scorched from an old accident, never sent. He reads his own younger handwriting and hears the lie inside it. Emotional beat: shame surfacing; the past stops being a place and becomes a person.

chapters.title: Imani, Unsent
chapters.summary: Imani's POV. Imani is fighting her own bank, and the town festival committee wants her historic bakery as festival grounds instead of a vendor stall. She's furious, capable, and quietly lonely. She doesn't know about the letter. Emotional beat: righteous exhaustion; she has built belonging alone and resents anyone who might take it.

chapters.title: Rival Ovens
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Wendell, unable to leave, leases the shop next to Imani's and enters the festival bake-off to win the right to keep both buildings standing. Their rivalry turns flirtatious, combative, electric. Emotional beat: heat; competition as the only language two proud people can safely speak.

chapters.title: The Muscle Remembers
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. A late-night power outage traps them in her kitchen; by candlelight they bake her grandmother's bread, and old intimacy resurfaces. Wendell almost confesses about the letter and retreats. Emotional beat: tenderness breaking through armor; the heart, he admits, was never trainable.

chapters.title: Power's Quiet Rot
chapters.summary: Imani's POV. The festival chair, Councilman Drey, offers Imani a deal: drop the bake-off and he'll save her bakery—by handing Wendell's café to demolition instead. She realizes the town's 'protection' has always been leverage. Emotional beat: disillusionment; she sees how belonging can be weaponized, and that Wendell once fled a town rigged the same way.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Imani, choosing integrity, tells Wendell about Drey's offer—and Wendell, panicking, accuses her of pity, then of being the reason he left, then confesses the letter exists. She demands to read it. He refuses. Emotional beat: the climax's fuse lit; his oldest defense—control—costs him the person he came back for.

chapters.title: The Reading
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, climax. Festival closing night: Drey announces the demolitions. Wendell takes the stage, reads the scorched letter aloud—naming his cowardice, his hunger for invisibility, his love—and publicly forgives the man who wrote it. The town sides with both bakers; Drey's deal collapses. Emotional beat: catharsis; vulnerability as the only power that doesn't corrupt.

chapters.title: Proof
chapters.summary: Imani's POV, then shared. Weeks later: the bakery and café are one shared kitchen, the festival saved, the letter framed behind the counter, burn mark and all. Imani gives Wendell her answer in bread and in words. Emotional beat: belonging chosen daily; love as proof that rises, is punched down, and rises again.
